purpose: Formalize (-1) ⇔R (+1) as symbolic recursive polarity preserved under bounded subdivision.
plain_language_definition: A candidate process-algebra law stating that symbolic exclusion-pole and continuation-pole relation is treated as indivisible under bounded subdivision.
core_interpretation: The relation between -1 and +1 is primary; the poles are not independently realizable process objects within this symbolic layer.

formal_seed.non_isolation_rule: No bounded subdivision may isolate pure -1 or pure +1 as an admissible standalone process term.
formal_seed.history_rule: Each subdivided ΩR_k preserves local residue-history sufficient to remain ⇔R-bound.
formal_seed.non_arithmetic_rule: -1 and +1 function as symbolic process poles, not ordinary numerical quantities.

allowed_uses: Expressing irreducible symbolic polarity in process algebra.
Modeling bounded subdivision without isolating independent poles.
Supporting the interpretation of ΩR as a recursive process unit.
Providing symbolic structure for exclusion-continuation coupling.
forbidden_uses: Claiming physical magnetism proves the law.
Claiming magnetic monopoles cannot exist physically.
Claiming universal scale invariance is proven.
Using this law as proof of physical reality.
Using this law to bypass formal theorem obligations.

relation_to_prior_patches.MPF-PALG-002: Uses ⇔R only as residue-bound recursive co-validity.
relation_to_prior_patches.MPF-PALG-003: Treats -1 as symbolic exclusion-pole and +1 as symbolic continuation-pole under non-arithmetic interpretation.
